claims.claim: Reviewers note that the anti-cheat system prevents the game from functioning properly on Linux and Steam Deck.

citations.review_text:
Game would not even get to the menu due to the new kernel level anti cheat update, which breaks things on Linux, Steamdeck etc.

The devs really need to fix this as it restricts you being able to even use the single player element.

I found a fix for others struggling to launch, use this as a launch command in game properties:

https_proxy=http://127.0.0.1:0 %command%

This should block the game trying to access the server so it can skip the anti cheat check to just play offline.
EAC borks Linux/Steam Deck. It boots you from the online session after a few minutes.

Game is more fun with a gamepad
But it is bricked on Linux
Meaning Steamdeck is not supported
(They could easily switch on PROTON SUPPORT but they didn't, and if they have files to download to tmp there is a proton file system they can download to)
Just saying "No steamdeck is playing our games so we wont bother" even tho they can't even Try the game
This game is fire but EAC is ass for linux users.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that character creation options are limited and result in models that look goofy.

citations.review_text:
Very boring gameplay thus far. Instead of pressing buttons to do attacks, it feels like I am pressing buttons to let a cutscene play out.
The sound mixing is pretty awful too. I don't care for the blarping music in the main hub, which is quite loud even when the music is nearly muted, but the music I actually enjoy in the game is almost inaudible. And I am not gonna change the music settings everytime I get through a loading screen, that would be too tedious.

Also, not being told that every race/gender combination has their own numerical strengths and weaknesses beyond what is told at the character creator is just obtuse. I thought it'd be fun to be a female saiyan brawler. Guess what, that's one of the worst combinations possible, which I had no way of knowing without coming upon it on the internet.

Minor nitpicks:
- completing a mission and my instructor being amazed at how good I am got old after the second time, let alone it happening every single time.
- there is no lip sync to speak off. Mouths move and words are said independent of another.

The create a character options are extremely lazy and makes it impossible to make a character that looks original without them ending up appearing goofy. For a game that is entirely based around your original character, I would want to make a character I am comfortable with. But good lord not only are the options limited, the quality of the models have just not been something that has been cared about by the developers. This game could have been really good, but it's just ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ lazy.

claims.claim: PvE side quests and combat feel repetitive after completing the main story.

citations.review_text:
Cool game if you're a Dragon Ball fan. After roughly 40 hours, the game starts to feel really repetitive if you don't do any online activities and since there aren't many players around anymore, or at least not many doing online content, don't expect any real online experience. All there is after completing the main story is to do a bunch of side quests again and again, and they pretty much all feel the same after a while. That's one of my main issues with the game. The PvE fights become really boring after the first few hours of excitement. You have to play a certain way, spamming your combos, and if you fail, the AI will spam its combos. That's pretty much it. Also, pray that your AI partners don't die before the end of the fight otherwise it can turn into a bullying simulator.

That being said, what makes this game so cool is obviously creating your own character, evolving in the Dragon Ball universe alongside its characters, while choosing your fighting style, outfits, and techniques. Definitely wait for a discount, especially since there are so much DLCs.
A fun dragonball fighter hampered by poor gameplay mechanics for repeat playthroughs.

That being said, what makes this game so cool is obviously creating your own character, evolving in the Dragon Ball universe alongside its characters, while choosing your fighting style, outfits, and techniques. Definitely wait for a discount, especially since there are so much DLCs.

I have to think the CPUs and combat system in this game are ragebait. I cannot think of any other reason why they would operate in such an insufferable manner. It's not even difficulty; It's easy-to-use, spammable actions requiring such unreasonably higher precision to counter. And any "fighting" game with unbreakable throws automatically goes into the party game category, as in not worth putting any kind of considerable time into learning. Movement is the most jank and inconsistent I've ever seen in a game with a pvp game, because sometimes you'll flick the stick and close quarters, and they'll smoothly rotate on axis to the foe, and others, they'll do a whole turn-around animation. In the air, there's many kinds of maneuvers to evade or pressure. None of which are possible on the ground.

The multiplayer modes are just as bad. In a setting where normal attacks are actually useless, you are forced to commit to stronger attacks. Stronger attacks mean more time spent in an idle state performing said attack. In a scenario where all this is the case, there's a bosses that can paralyze you at literally any moment they want, and if the whole team is stunned in this manner, gg. There's so much forced difficulty in the multiplayer modes, and an obscene amount of RNG.

I don't typically get angry when playing games. I play Tekken, and that game is known for being frustrating. But this game had me genuinely ready to put a hole through my monitor multiple times. From a character having a 6 second long cutscene for a basic (stupidly unbreakable) throw, certain ones spamming regular blasts, even at close range, instant evasive skills with a whole cutscene that you can't vanish out of, missions where the whole fight is held up and you can't take out any foes because "they're talking," and there being little to no reward for perfect guarding. claims.claim: Reviewers state that the Hero Colosseum minigame features a steep difficulty spike and requires significant grinding for figures.

citations.review_text: It was good until i got to Hero Colosseum, now i hope whoever designed all of this walks on LEGO for the rest of his life.

Dragon Ball Xenoverse 2 holds a very special spot in my heart. I used to play this game for hours and hours on end on the Xbox One, and when I saw it was on sale, I thought to myself, "I should get it and get all achievements."
It's a very fun Dragon Ball game and with Dragon Ball Xenoverse 3 coming out soon has made me appreciate the times I had played this in the past even more.

Now this game isn't all sunshine and rainbows, I do have very real complaints. The first of which is that for you to get all achievements, you do infact need to buy 3 DLCs. I was fine with it because I was already planning on buying them since I love this game, but it does suck that it's NEEDED for the 100%.
Now my main complaint, and what I think most people would complain about, is the Hero Colosseum. Oh my god, the Hero Colosseum is terrible. I don't have the words for how the difficulty skyrocketed almost every fight and how in order to get the figures you want, you need to spend a copious amount of time grinding loads of TP medals for the very low chance you get the figure you want and/or needed.

Besides those two complaints, which are completely optional, the game is a very fun and enjoyable experience for all Dragon Ball fans alike.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the combat system as featuring smooth, fluid movement and deep combo potential alongside a high skill ceiling.

citations.review_text:
[h1]9/10 - (almost) all a Dragon Ball fan could ask for![/h1]
[b]This game, finally coming toward the end of service after almost 10 years, with Dragon ball Xenoverse 3 on the way is currently one of the best dragon ball games to play.[/b] 
It stands the test of time with great gameplay, super fun customisation options, great post-game content. [hr][/hr]
[h2]The DLC Issue[/h2]
Where this game suffers, is in it's pure need for all the DLC to get the full experience. While the base game is great, you do miss a lot of the new story and characters if you choose not to pay extra. If you have the money, or can grab it bundled on sale I 100% recommend it. Otherwise, maybe hold off a little longer. 


[h2]Single player or multiplayer?[/h2]
I believe if you are a fan of both singleplayer and multiplayer, this game has something for you either way. While the PvP has its issues, the PvE is really where this game gets to shine. The optional quests are great fun in single player, but they really become elevated when you have a couple of friends to join in on the harder missions. 


[h2]Overall gameplay[/h2]
The combat in this game feels great! The movement is fluid, or easy to pick up while having a high skill ceiling at the same time. It is great being able to level up a character, and be able to pull off strong  supers and ultimate moves against difficult enemies or in PvP. 

This game has a simple gameplay loop.[b] Do a mission, get stronger, customise, repeat.[/b] In the base game, this loop is somewhat flexible, allowing you to do what you want to an extent to beat the main story, no grind necessary. However, in post game content and DLC, the grind does become quite intense. The item drops from missions are completely RNG so there is no telling how many times you might have to repeat a quest. This, however, is part of the game as it is very rewarding when you finally do get a new outfit / attack that is harder to obtain. 

[hr][/hr]
[h2]Should you buy it? [/h2]
Of course. I…

This game is best described as “expansive.” With the few DLCs that are required to complete all the achievements, there is still so much I haven’t done in the game, including getting one of my CACs to Level 200. 

However, your experience will depend on how enjoyable you find the main fighting and character customization mechanics. This game can be (and often is) a grind. You will be playing the same missions repeatedly, sometimes for hours, to either obtain a Skill, outfit, or other item, or obtain the TP medals to purchase them. 

First, combat feels smooth enough for you to perform satisfying combos with a variety of the game’s moves. Advanced tech, such as using a ki blast after your last hit to greatly reduce your ending lag and extend combos (ki cancelling), ensures that there is somewhat of a skill and knowledge gap while still being approachable. Most of the interactions are turned-based, with the attacking player often using Ki to perform stronger Super and Ultimate attacks to deal damage, and the defending player using Stamina to Z-Vanish or to use an Evasive Skill to get out of danger and start their assault. Both players must predict what the other will do to punish any weak spots or mistakes that one side makes. My biggest issue is that to perform a stamina break, a key move to extending combos, I found the control stick inconsistent when trying to input towards the enemy. I mostly played the game using the D-Pad, which provided more precision.

There is also a huge roster, with hundreds of characters and presets to choose from, spanning from Z, GT, and Super. Although there is some overlap in moves and animations, there’s often enough to differentiate between them in terms of how to best use their light and medium attacks, stamina breaks, Skills, and transformations to win a fight. 

Thankfully, the grind does feel (mostly) worth it to customize your custom character, who is the protagonist of the story. You can choose between six races (with some havi…

Dragon Ball Xenoverse 2 is a great example of a game that has stayed alive thanks to its incredibly long post-launch support. At first, the combat system seems fairly simple, but with practice it reveals surprising depth, allowing you to chain together combos and creatively mix different special attacks.
Character creation and progression are another highlight, offering plenty of customization options to match your preferred playstyle. The graphics are decent at best, but the PC version is still the best-looking release across all platforms. The soundtrack is serviceable, though not particularly memorable.
The biggest downside is the overwhelming amount of DLC. There are simply too many packs, and many of them add too little content to justify their price.

Pros:
+ Excellent long-term post-launch support.
+ Deep and rewarding combat system.
+ Great character customization and progression.

Cons:
- Graphics are only decent.
- Soundtrack is just okay.
- Too many DLC packs with too little value.
